questions.question: What is the core idea behind prompt refinement for code generation?
choices: Making prompts as short as possible to save tokens
Transforming vague or incomplete instructions into precise, structured prompts that give the AI enough context to generate correct, working code
Using the same generic prompt for all coding tasks
Removing all constraints from the prompt to give the AI creative freedom
questions.explanation: Prompt refinement converts ambiguous requests into structured instructions with clear inputs, outputs, constraints, and examples. The more precise the prompt, the closer the AI's output matches what you actually need.

questions.question: Which of the following makes a prompt 'bad' for code generation?
choices: Specifying the programming language and data types
Being vague about the desired behavior and edge cases
questions.explanation: Vague prompts force the AI to guess at behavior, leading to incorrect implementations. Good prompts specify: what the function does, expected inputs/outputs, edge cases to handle, error behavior, and any constraints.

questions.question: What is the key benefit of using structured prompts with explicit sections (input, output, constraints, examples)?
choices: Structured prompts take up more space and are always better
Structure eliminates ambiguity by separating concerns, making it easy for the AI to address each aspect and for humans to verify completeness
Structured prompts are only needed for complex algorithms
AI models cannot parse structured text formats
questions.explanation: Structured prompts with labeled sections force you to think through each aspect (behavior, constraints, edge cases, format) and give the AI a clear template to follow. This reduces ambiguity and makes output more predictable and correct.
